Operational continuity is backed by <cite id="3">28.5 months of working capital reserves</cite>. On the ground, partner reporting indicates that funding facilitated <cite id="4">400 medical procedures and surgeries</cite> as well as <cite id="4">240 trained teachers for inclusive education</cite> in 2024.
rich_narrative.summary: Friends of KDSP supports children with Down syndrome in Pakistan by funding healthcare services, therapies, and early childhood interventions <cite id="4">through local partner networks</cite>. Operating as a US-based funding organization, it reported <cite id="3">$1,147,717 in total revenue in FY2025</cite>. Limiting factors constrain its overall score profile, including a <cite id="3">70.2% program expense ratio in FY2025</cite>, which sits below the <cite id="1">75% industry standard</cite> and the <cite id="1">89.5% peer median</cite>. Additionally, the organization lacks a <cite id="4">documented theory of change</cite> and external impact evaluations to verify long-term outcomes. Bright spots exist in its operations, such as maintaining <cite id="3">28.5 months of working capital reserves</cite> and supporting network services for <cite id="4">2,200 individuals with Down syndrome</cite>.
